title: INTELLIGENCE
subtitle: Design Knowledge Between Human and AI

editors.name: Joaquín Ángel Martínez Moya
editors.affiliation: Universitat Jaume I, Castelló de la Plana

intro: Palladianist Vol. 3 explores how technology and artificial intelligence can disseminate scientific knowledge and support design and creative methods.

The issue looks at digital museology and at the role architectural representation can play within it, and at how multimedia languages can support design. It asks whether new tools remove barriers to knowledge or create new ones.
topics: Drawing as an accessible design language, from Palladio's treatise to diagrams and easy-to-read formats
Multisensory translations of heritage: tactile drawings, 3D-printed models, haptic, sound and olfactory devices
Survey and digital modelling for the accessibility of historic places: HBIM, digital twins, wayfinding
Digital museology and Extended Reality: virtual and phygital museums
AI for the interpretation and mediation of heritage: image description, sign language, simplified and multilingual content
Intangible heritage, local identities and participatory knowledge, including co-design with communities and people with disabilities
Inclusive education and learning through drawing
contributionTypes: Methodological reflections on design, teaching and emerging technologies
review: All contributions undergo double-blind peer review.
languages: Papers may be submitted for review in English, Italian or Spanish. Accepted papers are published in English.
